Lesson2.3-the-executable-zoo 2.3-the-executable-zoo

Why models are newly central

Part 1 derived the Modeling Thesis from three facts about a coding fleet.

The upkeep that constrained MBSE, a fleet now pays cheaply

Model-based systems engineering did not fail on its ideas.

The fewer-tokens leg — a navigation pilot

The *fewer-tokens* leg is directly measurable.

The shared machinery that holds any view true

Most of the catalogue's method models belong to no single view.

Derive and join; do not repeat

A model here is **derived** — from the code, or the code from it — never kept beside the code as a parallel document.

State the derivation direction

A model and the code stay equal by derivation, and derivation runs in one of two directions.

Descriptive maps and intent-bearing models

The purest model-from-code artifact is the repository graph a growing class of tools now hands a coding agent: a parser walks the repository into a persistent, queryable graph of its entities and relations — functions, classes, imports, calls, endpoints, schemas, tables — so the agent reasons through the graph instead of re-reading raw files.

Keep map and territory equal — traceability

The model is the **map**; the code is the **territory**.

How a model stays trustworthy

Drift enforcement is where a model stops merely helping the fleet reason and the environment begins refusing to let model and code silently disagree.

A model is its schema plus its checked predicates

Read that as one operational equation: **an executable model is its schema plus its checked predicates.** Fields (b) and (c) of the reference template below give the **structured model** — records, edges, state machines.

How to read a model page

Part II teaches modeling by leading each section with an engineering question; the **appendix** documents each model with a uniform five-field reference template, so a reader who has read one reference page can read any of them on reflex.

How much governance is enough

Which raises the real question: how much governance is enough?

Example — Spotify Migration at fleet scale stays incremental: you target a change, schedule it across the estate, drain it, and keep a human on the exceptions. Spotify is the evidence it holds at organizational size — a fleet-wide migration that once drew in hundreds of teams and ran for weeks is now scoped by one engineer over a few days, the tooling targeting and scheduling the work while agents implement it concurrently and the engineer watches the fleet and handles the exceptions rather than typing each change [cite:spotify2026honk]. What to imitate is the placement, not the tool: put the scarce human decision upstream — *what, where, when, whether* — and let the environment carry the change onward, the same move the strategies above run at a single-subsystem grain. The takeaway is that scale does not undo the incremental discipline; it raises the payoff, so the move that repays weeks on one subsystem repays far more across a fleet.

Lesson4.3-validating-change 4.3-validating-change

What does it mean to validate a change?

To validate a change is to assemble evidence that it satisfies its obligations — and to refuse it otherwise.

The model as oracle

None of the individual validation techniques in this chapter is new.

The move: a generator hunts a counterexample to a model

Before the three members, the shared shape.

After this section — the reader can
  • applyAfter this section, the reader can apply the one move behind property testing, fuzzing, and fuzz-MBSE: a generator hunting a counterexample to a stated model. derived
Fuzz + MBSE: the structured model becomes the oracle

The richest form of validation-from-a-model turns the model itself into the judge.

Choosing the validation technique

Models expose intent and metrics measure degree; **validators** are the machine-read checks that consume both and return a verdict.

Property-based testing: the invariant is the oracle

In property-based testing the author writes the law and the machine hunts the counterexample [cite: claessen2000quickcheck].

Fuzzing: the contract is "never crash, never corrupt"

Where a property test asks a rich question of inputs drawn from an authored domain, fuzzing asks a coarser question of arbitrary, mutated ones.

Coverage: did the validation explore the claim?

A validator answers a yes/no obligation; a **metric** answers a question of degree, and degree is its own kind of evidence.

Deterministic admission

These checks are deterministic sensors, machine-read — and they **become hard governance when their verdicts control admission**, wired as a commit gate that refuses the merge.

Why this matters in the agentic era

Autonomous development does not change *what* engineering evidence is.

Industrial example

The move is one a team can copy: generate evidence built to falsify a claim, and admit only the claim that survives.

  • analyzeAfter this section, the reader can analyze a hard, deterministic metric at the level where the decision lives — reading cold-start latency one level deeper to name runtime initialization rather than scale-from-zero, computing a longest-path worst case over a service graph, and feeding the number into a structured deployment model a recompute tool consumes. derived
The flagship: coverage measured one level deeper

Now the middle of the spectrum: the "measure one level deeper" rule applied to the number that most often gets it wrong.

After this section — the reader can
  • applyAfter this section, the reader can compute coverage measured one level deeper — joining a traceability graph's claim-to-anchor edges with the coverage oracle so the metric counts model claims instead of lines, names an unexercised invariant instead of a percentage, and reports an honest exercised/unmeasurable/out-of-surface breakdown. derived
The dual: draining unmodelled code

The flagship metric had a blind spot: it measured model→code, so code with no model at all stayed invisible to it — and this dual is what finds it.

The soft end: doc-derived tests

Slide to the far end of the spectrum, where the metric stops being a number a threshold can act on and becomes a judgment a human has to make.

After this section — the reader can
  • analyzeAfter this section, the reader can classify a soft metric — a doc-derived test's coverage-of-doc-claims — as one that aims a reader rather than deciding, recognize why its softness is inseparable from a readiness judgment about the seam, and see why wiring it to a blocking gate manufactures hollow tests. derived
The model runs the machinery

The hard end and the flagship follow the same pattern.

After this section — the reader can
  • understandAfter this section, the reader can explain why the MBSE models are consumed at runtime to produce the metrics — the cold-start numbers and the coverage graph both read at check time — so a component-distance grade read from the model drives a pre-commit gate three ways, the model being the machinery rather than a picture of it. derived
A compact reference

[ref:metrics-table] collects every metric — the decision each drives, where it sits on the hard-soft axis, and who reads it.
